title: How teachers are remaking classrooms for the AI age
gist: Forum commentary on a Reuters piece describing US teachers replacing homework with in-class writing, oral exams and handwritten work in response to student AI use. Nenni argues assessment must shift to the process of reasoning, with accessibility safeguards, AI literacy and teacher support.

insights.claim: Per Reuters, American teachers are replacing some homework with classroom writing, oral examinations and practical activities, and some are returning to handwritten work, in response to students' AI use.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI is driving a structural shift away from take-home assessment.
insights.quote: Teachers are replacing some homework with classroom writing, oral examinations and practical activities that reveal students’ understanding.

insights.claim: Nenni argues a polished essay or correct answer offers limited evidence of understanding when software can produce it instantly, so education must emphasize the process of learning.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Credentialing based on output artifacts loses signal value in the AI era.
insights.quote: A polished essay or correct answer offers limited evidence of understanding when software can produce it instantly.

insights.claim: Oral exams may disadvantage anxious students or those needing processing time, and handwritten tasks can block learners relying on assistive technology.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni

insights.claim: Students need practice questioning generated answers, checking evidence, recognizing uncertainty and disclosing when they used automated assistance.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI literacy curricula may become a standard education requirement.

insights.claim: Successful adaptation depends on giving teachers support, time and shared guidance, and on preserving meaningful human interaction while choosing technology for specific purposes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Implementation capacity, not technology, is the bottleneck for schools.
insights.quote: teachers need support, time and shared guidance to redesign learning effectively
